title: Restore eval output parity for large customer after inference config inheritance change
creator: Ava Martinez
description: A major enterprise customer reported that a previously stable eval suite started producing inconsistent outputs after we rolled runtime-1.22. The behavior differs across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments: Hosted saw an immediate regression, Dedicated customers with tenant overrides were partially protected, and some Private customers observed no change due to pinned configs. The regression manifests as extra trailing tokens and occasional premature cutoff of reference answers, causing failing automated evals and broken downstream scoring.
investigation_notes: 2025-03-05 - Customer support: initial escalation from AcmeHealth showing automated eval suite failure rates up 18% since 2025-03-03.
2025-03-06 - Triaged: narrowed to recent runtime-1.22 release that changed inference-config inheritance and introduced a new default for termination precedence.

Repro steps: use customer's prompt set (attached in links), run model-v3.1 under runtime-1.21 vs runtime-1.22 with identical model weights and deployment region, compare token sequences and termination signals.

Telemetry: we see an increase in requests that return a termination sequence after additional sampling steps (trailing filler tokens) for Hosted; Dedicated tenant overrides show expected behavior for tenants that had explicit termination sentinel set.

Root cause hypothesis: config inheritance was altered so that a new global default for sampling/termination took precedence over deployment-level tenant overrides when requests are routed through the new smart-routing path. Private installs that had configs pinned were unaffected.
Observed variance: per-prompt differences amplified for prompts relying on exact stop delimiters; open-ended prompts show token drift but less visible impact.
Related telemetry panels: runtime-termination-events-dashboard, eval-failures-by-tenant, request-trace-samples (links below)
Relevant commits: runtime config merge change in GH#4154; sampling default tweak in GH#4178.
mitigation: Hotfix deployed to Hosted: toggle to enforce legacy termination precedence for affected customers (--legacy-termination-precedence=true). Applied for AcmeHealth and two other customers on 2025-03-07; customer confirmed reduction in eval failures to baseline.
Dedicated: notified SEs with instructions to apply tenant-level override (console > Tenant Settings > Inference > Termination Precedence = explicit). Created automation script for infra teams.
Private: published a patch bundle and release notes for operators; advised customers to apply if they upgrade to 1.22.
Monitoring: added temporary alert for delta in termination-event rate > 5% over baseline per tenant.
Customer communication: sent incident summary and workaround steps; scheduled follow-up demo with AcmeHealth for 2025-03-13.
rollback_plan: If hotfix is insufficient, revert runtime-1.22 config inheritance change on Hosted for affected clusters via canary rollback: revert GH#4154 in canary, monitor eval pass-rate and latency for 24h, then expand to remaining canaries.
Rollback steps documented in Confluence (link below) and runbook updated for on-call.
fix_details: Implement definitive fix to config merge and precedence order: request-level overrides > tenant-level overrides > deployment defaults > global defaults. Ensure termination sentinel settings cannot be implicitly overridden by new smart-routing defaults.
Add explicit field 'termination_mode' with allowed values [legacy|strict|auto] to avoid implicit behavior changes.
Code changes: runtime/config_merge.go and routing/handler.go. Unit tests and integration tests included in PR GH#4221.
Backward compatibility: when 'termination_mode' is absent, use tenant/deployment fallback and emit telemetry event to identify customers relying on implicit behavior.
Estimate: 8 points; target merge by 2025-03-14 and staged rollout in runtime-1.22.1.
Add per-tenant canary flags so we can opt customers into new behavior with a switch in the Console.
qa_plan: Create end-to-end harness that runs customer's eval set against current and candidate runtimes and asserts exact token-wise equality for termination-sensitive prompts.
Add regression test cases to CI that include prompts with multiple termination delimiters and nested function responses.
Run smoke tests on Hosted canaries for 48h before promoting patch to all clusters.
Manual verification: Redwood Solutions engineer will validate with AcmeHealth's eval harness and sign off.
Acceptance criteria: eval failure rate returns to baseline (within 2%), no increase in request latency beyond 5ms P95.
